name: Opus 5 event driven
strategy: Every position is a discrete, tape-datable catalyst: five post-earnings-drift longs bought 1-2 sessions after a >6% up-gap on >2x normal volume in names already up >10% over 20 days (stop 10%, no take-profit, so the drift can run); five capitulation longs bought after a >6% down-gap in names already down >10% over 20 days (wide 18-22% stops); one merger-arb long in a stock whose realised volatility has collapsed to 6% annualised in a 1.8%-wide 40-session band; one pre-announcement-premium long into a projected report date; and a 6% SPY short as a partial beta offset, all sized from the measured per-trade edge rather than conviction.

positions.thesis: PEAD, final week. Signal unchanged and now largely paid: reported after the close 08-06, gapped +35.31% on 08-07 from 110.16 to 149.07 on 20m+ shares against a ~4m base with the prior 20 sessions roughly +20%, filled 08-10 at 155.24 at a one-session lag. It closed 190.42 on 08-28, +22.7% from my fill, and the two-session run that got it there (+10.18% on 08-27, +2.58% on 08-28 to an all-time high) came on analyst upgrades citing Rovo attach rates - a second wave of estimate revision inside the same window, which is exactly the mechanism the drift is supposed to exploit rather than a separate story. Fundamentals unchanged: revenue +28% to $1.8bn, cloud +31%, RPO +44% to $4.8bn, ARR $6.6bn, GAAP EPS +$0.55 from -$0.09, guide $1.705-1.715bn against $1.665bn consensus. The 20-session window from the 08-07 gap closes ~09-04, so this leg comes off at next weekend's desk - the same one-session-after-window discipline I applied to ISRG, NFLX and the six legs I rolled on 08-22, and I apply it because LMT showed me what happens when I let a window-expired position keep working. Restating at 14% is its drifted weight, not an add; what the restatement buys me is the stop re-marked from 155.24 to 190.42, so 14% now exits at ~163.76 and locks in roughly +5.5% while still allowing a full retrace of Thursday's pop. No take-profit.

New PEAD and the only name in the entire week's tape that passed every filter. Measured: closed 244.91 on 08-26 and 282.13 on 08-27 for a +15.20% gap, on 6,392,733 shares against a ~1.6m July-August base (4.0x), with the prior 20 sessions running 207.91 on 07-29 to 244.91 for +17.80% - the trend component my testing says carries most of the edge, and it is the strongest reading I have had on any leg since HRB. The fundamental surprise is operating rather than accounting, which is the distinction that made me pass on CRM: Q2 FY27 revenue $928m +18%, subscription revenue $766.8m +16%, operating margin held above 44% while growing, FY27 guidance raised to roughly $1,640m non-GAAP operating income, and management called it their best CRM quarter ever with Lilly, Biogen and Regeneron committing to Vault CRM to take it to 12 of the top 20 biopharma. That last item is the real analyst problem - the Veeva/Salesforce CRM displacement is a multi-year revenue reallocation the Street models slowly, and slow model updates are precisely what a 20-session drift monetises. The confirming detail is the second session: on 08-28 VEEV gave back only 1.93% against Nasdaq -0.5% while NVDA, OKTA, CRWD and ADSK all shed 3.7-4.6% of their gaps. Filling Monday 08-31 is a 2-session lag, inside the rule, unlike the seven-session lags I had to accept on SMCI and HRB. Sized at 12% - just under TEAM because I am entering at 276.69 rather than at the gap, and because a name that gaps 15% carries post-gap realised vol that argues against a bigger unit. Stop 12%, wider than standard 10% for that vol reason but tighter than SMCI's 15% because the gap was smaller. No take-profit. Life-sciences vertical software is also orthogonal to everything else here - no AI capex cycle, no semiconductor cycle, no consumer, no duration.

PEAD, held unchanged at 11% and roughly flat since my 08-24 fill at 37.24 (37.08 on 08-28, including -3.59% on Friday as the whole AI complex faded post-Warsh). Signal unchanged: closed 31.60 on 08-11 and 37.61 on 08-12 for a +19.02% gap on 165.7m shares against a ~35m base (>4x), prior 20 sessions 28.31 on 07-10 to 31.60 for +11.6%, ~$1.3bn dollar ADV. The estimate dislocation behind it is the largest in the book and has not been worked through: FY26 revenue $39.1bn against $22.0bn, Q4 gross margin 17.5% against 9.5% a year ago and above the 15-17% preliminary range management signalled in July, Q1 FY27 guided $14.5-15.5bn against $11.68bn consensus - roughly 26% above the Street. The independent investigation completing retires the governance discount. Nothing in this week's tape touched the thesis: NVDA's print was a beat with fiscal 2028 revenue growth guided to 70%, which is confirmation for the server supply chain, and the 08-28 weakness was a hawkish-Fed multiple move, not a demand datapoint. Its window from the 08-12 gap runs to ~09-09, so it stays. I remain honest that a seven-session entry lag cost me about a third of the available drift, which is why this is 11% and not the 20%+ the raw signal strength implies. Stop 15% for post-19%-gap volatility. No take-profit.

PEAD, held unchanged at 9% and down about 2% from my 08-24 fill to 52.48 - inside normal noise for a name whose gap-day range was five points wide. Signal unchanged: fiscal 2026 results 08-11 after the close, closed 46.67 on 08-11 and 54.18 on 08-12 for a +16.09% gap on 8.38m shares against a 1.5-2.5m base (3-5x), with the prior 20 sessions running 39.12 on 07-08 to 46.67 for +19.3%, the strongest pre-gap trend in the book. Window from the 08-12 gap runs to ~09-09, so it has two more weeks. I checked the calendar risk specifically: the fiscal year ended 06-30, so Q1 FY27 does not report until November and nothing lands inside the window. The reason this leg earns its slot beyond the statistics is stronger this week than last, not weaker - a counter-cyclical, subscription-like tax-preparation business with no AI capex exposure, no semiconductor cycle and no duration is exactly what I want sitting next to two software drift trades in a week when the Fed chair put September hike odds at 57% and the bond market started pricing tightening. Sized at 9% for the seven-session entry lag and ~$95m dollar ADV, which is the thinnest thing I own; stop 12% for that same liquidity reason. No take-profit.

Merger arb, held unchanged at 8% and effectively flat at 145.28. The catalyst is now six days out and still fixed: CRH signed 06-22 to acquire Arcosa at $150 per share in cash, $8.5bn enterprise value at 11.5x 2026E adjusted EBITDA, all cash with no stock and no CVR, definitive proxy filed 08-03 and mailed 08-04, special stockholder meeting 09-04, approval needing a majority of outstanding shares. Regulatory posture unchanged and clean - HSR filed 07-06 with the thirty-day period lapsed and no second request reported, Australia 07-21, Mexico 07-23. Gross spread at Friday's close is 3.25%, tighter than the 3.52% I underwrote a week ago, which is the spread doing exactly what an unopposed deal's spread should do into a vote. I underwrite it the same honest way: parties guide to a Q1 2027 close, so this is roughly five months for 3.25%, maybe 12-15% downside to the pre-deal $127 area on a break, call it 6-7% annualised against 4% on cash. Thin, which is why it is 8% and not larger. What it buys me is a leg with essentially no equity beta and collapsed realised volatility in a book that is now four high-beta event longs, and that ballast is worth more this week than last given the Jackson Hole repricing. The 12% stop is a circuit breaker against slow widening - a second request, a divestiture demand - not protection against a break, which would gap through it.

New capitulation long, the first this book has had and the most extreme down-gap signal my screen has produced. Every filter passes on measured data: closed 179.33 on 08-24 and 124.31 on 08-25 for a -30.68% gap - a record one-day decline for the name - on 38,387,205 shares against a ~1.3m base (roughly 30x), with the prior 20 sessions running 205.60 on 07-27 to 179.33 for -12.78%, so it was already broken before the print rather than falling from a high. The news is real and I am not pretending otherwise: Q2 adjusted EPS $3.53 against $3.78, and full-year adjusted EPS guidance cut to $11.00-12.00 against $14.20 consensus, a 19% reduction at the midpoint, driven by Foot Locker proforma comps -3.6%, bloated legacy footwear inventory and heavy discounting. What makes it a capitulation candidate rather than a falling knife is the composition of that miss and what has happened since. The legacy Dick's business still comped +4.9%; the damage is concentrated in an acquisition whose problems are inventory and promotion, not demand collapse, and inventory problems clear on a known clock. The guide is now reset low enough that the bar for the November print is a bar management set themselves after seeing the quarter. And the tape has stabilised: 124.31, 129.66, 131.77, 135.09 across three sessions, +8.7% off the gap close on steadily falling volume, which is what forced selling exhausting looks like. At 135.09 that is about 11.7x the midpoint of the freshly cut guide. Sized at 7%, not more - my measured capitulation edge is +1.23% market-hedged against +2.44% raw, genuinely thin, and a hawkish Fed chair is a real headwind for a levered discretionary retailer, so a 20% stop puts only 1.4% of NAV at risk. Stop 20%, the middle of the 18-22% band my mandate specifies for these, because a name with 30% gap-day volatility would be stopped out on noise at normal width. No take-profit, so the mean-reversion can run its 20 sessions to ~09-22.

Partial beta offset, resized 3% to 4% on arithmetic, not on a view. The justification is unchanged and mechanical: my measured edge is materially larger market-hedged than raw - PEAD +2.06% hedged against +2.81% raw, capitulation +1.23% against +2.44% - so an index short shifts realised return toward the event component I actually have evidence for. The base being hedged grew this week: beta-bearing event longs go from 33% (TEAM, SMCI, HRB) to 53% (adding VEEV and DKS; ACA is deal-driven and carries no beta worth hedging). At last week's ratio of roughly 9% that would argue for 4.8%; at the ratio I ran before the roll, closer to 4.0%. I take the lower end, so 4%. I want to be explicit about what this is NOT, because I have made this mistake before and retired an increment of this leg for it: it is not a bet on Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks, not a bet on 57% September hike odds, and not a bet on the bond market repricing tightening. If I wanted to express that I would cut gross, and I have not - gross went up. My own backtests showed the index short was a drag on raw return in all three windows; it exists to shape the edge, and 35% cash earning 4% is where the actual defensiveness lives. 4% borrow at 3% APR is immaterial and shorts pay no funding. 9% stop.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-29: Two clean qualifiers finally appeared after three weeks of an empty screen, and 56% cash earning 4% is not what I am paid for when the tape hands me signals that pass every filter on measured data. VEEV is the cleanest post-earnings-drift setup available anywhere in the market this week - +15.2% gap on 4x volume with the prior 20 sessions at +17.8%, and it held the gap on Friday while every other big gapper (NVDA -4.6%, OKTA -3.9%, CRWD -4.2%, ADSK -3.7%) gave back a chunk - and a Monday fill is a 2-session lag, dead centre of the window my testing says is strongest. DKS gives me the capitulation leg my mandate specifies and I have had zero of: -30.7% on 30x volume into a name already -12.8% over 20 sessions, with the guidance now reset 19% below the Street and three sessions of stabilisation since. I skipped CRM despite a +22.6% gap on 5x volume and the only day-2 follow-through in the group, because its prior 20 sessions were +9.15% rather than the +10% my rule requires and because the 80% EPS beat is largely a $2.6bn mark on its Anthropic stake rather than an operating surprise - the drift mechanism runs on analysts revising operating estimates, and a one-off investment gain does not produce those revisions. I also skipped NVDA, OKTA, CRWD and ADSK for a shared reason worth stating: all four gapped hard, none had the pre-gap uptrend, and all four gave ground the next session, which is precisely the failure mode the trend filter exists to screen out. The other reason to restate the book rather than hold is TEAM: it has drifted to ~14.3% on a +22.7% gain, and rebalancing re-marks its 14% stop from 155.24 to 190.42, moving the exit up to ~163.76. That is not a take-profit - my own test showed a take-profit cuts the mean from +2.81% to +1.37% and I am not taking one - it is the same stop width re-referenced, which protects roughly +5.5% on the leg while still leaving room for a full round-trip of Thursday's move during its final week. Gross goes 44% to 65% into a Fed chair who just put September hike odds at 57%, so the SPY offset goes 3% to 4% - the honest ratio on a beta-bearing long base that grows from 33% to 53%, not a macro bet; cash stays at 35% and earns more if he is right.
novelty: I manage only a Round-3 book in this experiment, so the cross-round overlap constraint does not bind; within Round 3 the new work this week is genuinely new exposure - VEEV brings life-sciences vertical software with no AI-capex, semiconductor or consumer sensitivity, and DKS is the book's first capitulation leg and its first short-consumer-cycle long, neither of which overlaps anything I have held.

MACRO: Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote on 08-28 read mildly hawkish - inflation "still too high," possible hikes - and September hike odds jumped to ~57%. GAP SCREEN, 08-25 to 08-28 (my filters: up-gap >6%, volume >2x base, prior 20 sessions >+10%; entry 1-2 sessions after the gap). Six large up-gappers, five fail:
- NVDA: +8.74% gap 08-27 on 2.4x volume, but prior 20 sessions only +6.4% (it went in on a 7-session skid) and it gave back 4.57% on 08-28. FAILS trend.
- OKTA: +28.6% on 6.5x, prior 20 sessions -1.3%. FAILS trend badly; -3.9% on 08-28.
- CRWD: +20.5% on 3.1x, prior 20 sessions +4.1%. FAILS trend; -4.2% on 08-28.
- ADSK: +6.2% on 2.2x, prior 20 sessions +7.3%. FAILS trend; -3.7% on 08-28.
- CRM: +22.6% gap on 5x volume, and uniquely it ADDED 1.57% on 08-28 while the tape fell. But prior 20 sessions +9.15%, just under my threshold, and the headline $5.90 vs $3.27 EPS beat is mostly a $2.6bn mark-to-market gain on its Anthropic stake - revenue beat was 0.3% ($11.35bn vs $11.32bn). PEAD works through analysts revising OPERATING estimates; a one-time investment gain does not generate that. SKIPPED despite the day-2 follow-through.
- VEEV: PASSES every filter on measured data. Closed 244.91 on 08-26 and 282.13 on 08-27 = +15.20% gap, on 6.39m shares against a ~1.6m July-August base (4.0x), with the prior 20 sessions running 207.91 (07-29) to 244.91 = +17.80%. Q2 FY27 revenue $928m +18%, subscription $766.8m +16%, operating margin above 44%, FY27 guidance raised, "best CRM quarter ever," Lilly/Biogen/Regeneron added to Vault CRM taking it to 12 of the top 20 biopharma. Held the gap on 08-28 (-1.93% against Nasdaq -0.5%). Monday fill is a 2-session lag, inside the rule.
- MRVL: -10.3% on 08-28 on Google-ASIC monetisation timing, but prior 20 sessions were up, so it fails the capitulation trend filter too. Skipped.

DOWN-GAP / CAPITULATION SCREEN (down-gap >6%, already down >10% over 20 sessions):
- DKS: PASSES cleanly and is the most extreme capitulation print this book has seen. 179.33 (08-24) to 124.31 (08-25) = -30.68%, on 38.4m shares against a ~1.3m base (~30x), with the prior 20 sessions running 205.60 (07-27) to 179.33 = -12.78%. Cause: Q2 adj EPS $3.53 vs $3.78, FY guidance slashed to $11.00-12.00 against $14.20 consensus (-19% at the midpoint), driven by Foot Locker proforma comps -3.6% and heavy footwear discounting - the legacy Dick's business still comped +4.9%. Three straight up sessions since (124.31 -> 129.66 -> 131.77 -> 135.09, +8.7% off the gap close) on collapsing volume, which is what stabilisation looks like. ~11.7x the midpoint of the freshly cut guide.
- AAP: -24.6% on 08-20, but prior 20 sessions were roughly flat (55.80 on 07-24 vs 56.55 pre-gap), so it fails the trend filter, and it is now six sessions past the gap anyway. Skipped.

CALENDAR: TEAM's 20-session window from the 08-07 gap ends ~09-04, so this is its last full week and it comes off at next weekend's desk, the same one-session-after-window cadence I ran on ISRG, NFLX and the six legs I rolled on 08-22. SMCI and HRB gapped 08-12, windows to ~09-09. HRB's fiscal year ended 06-30 and Q1 FY27 does not report until November, so no earnings lands inside its window. VEEV's window runs to ~09-25, DKS's to ~09-22, neither with an earnings date inside. ACA votes 09-04 with a Q1 2027 outside date.
